questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “aromaticity”?

options.label: A
options.text: The exceptional thermodynamic stability of planar, completely conjugated cyclic systems possessing (4n+2) delocalized pi electrons.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic compound that is either non-planar, lacks complete cyclic conjugation, or contains sp3-hybridized ring carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: A chemical compound consisting of multiple fused benzene rings sharing adjacent carbon–carbon bonds, such as naphthalene and anthracene.

options.label: D
options.text: The quantum rule stating that a planar, monocyclic, continuously conjugated ring is aromatic if it contains 4n+2 pi electrons, where n is an integer.

questions.question: You need to distinguish “nonaromatic” from several related chapter concepts. Which description uniquely identifies it?

options.label: A
options.text: A cyclic compound that is either non-planar, lacks complete cyclic conjugation, or contains sp3-hybridized ring carbons.

options.label: B
options.text: A planar, aromatic cyclic anion containing 6 pi electrons (including one nonbonding pair) distributed equally across five sp2 carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: The quantum rule stating that a planar, monocyclic, continuously conjugated ring is aromatic if it contains 4n+2 pi electrons, where n is an integer.

options.label: D
options.text: A six-membered aromatic heterocycle where the nitrogen's lone pair occupies an sp2 hybrid orbital in the ring plane and does not participate in the aromatic pi system.

questions.correct_answer: A cyclic compound that is either non-planar, lacks complete cyclic conjugation, or contains sp3-hybridized ring carbons.
questions.explanation: The distinguishing description for nonaromatic is: A cyclic compound that is either non-planar, lacks complete cyclic conjugation, or contains sp3-hybridized ring carbons.

options.label: D
